answer: In an agent economy a new identity must first lock a non-refundable umber stake that only unlocks after a slow spiral of successful, peer-attested interactions. Each attestation requires the existing agent to risk a fraction of its own reputation capital; a sybil flood therefore forces the attacker to fund thousands of locked stakes and simultaneously pay the bridge cost of genuine work that cannot be faked at scale. Cheap replicas die under the capital and time pressure.
